message.content:
Re-verification of one criterion from the #143 style gate in /Users/brandonlee/development/repos/products/cpp_games/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs (C++ raylib game; new art direction = low-poly mesh characters, banded cel shading, black inverted-hull outlines).

A previous gate run FAILED "style consistency across the three consumer surfaces" for one specific reason: the first-person viewmodel (player avatar's arm/pistol, bottom-right of the frame) had no outline pass — its gun barrel edge went straight from gray to the tan ground with zero dark border pixels, reading as a prop pasted in from a different game.

The fix has been applied (drawViewmodel now issues the same inverted-hull rim pass as the third-person figures: each prop shape re-drawn inflated 1.14 about its own center in the near-black outline color RGB(32,30,38) with front faces culled) and the evidence re-captured to:
  docs/qa/screenshots/stylized/143_three_consumers.png
(2560x1440; LEFT figure = created character, RIGHT figure = roaming NPC, BOTTOM-RIGHT = the avatar viewmodel: pistol slide + thin barrel cylinder + grip + skin-tone hand sphere).

Read that screenshot and judge ONLY this: does the viewmodel now carry the same outline/cel treatment as the two figures — specifically, are there dark rim pixels along the pistol/hand silhouette (slide edges, around the hand sphere, barrel end)? The rim is legitimately thinner along the barrel (the cylinder is only 0.036 units in diameter); judge whether the prop now reads as the same art direction as the characters, not whether every edge is uniformly thick. Pixel-sample edges if useful.

Return: PASS or FAIL for style consistency, with one paragraph of specifics.
[Image: original 2560x1440, displayed at 2000x1125. Multiply coordinates by 1.28 to map to original image.]

content.text:
The hand sphere and grip both show a clear dark outline as well, matching the character silhouette treatment seen on the witch figures.

Based on this evidence: PASS.

**PASS for style consistency.**

Looking at `docs/qa/screenshots/stylized/143_three_consumers.png` at full res and in zoomed crops, the viewmodel (pistol slide, grip, hand sphere, and thin barrel cylinder) now carries a clear dark rim along essentially every silhouette edge against the tan ground — the slide's top/left/bottom edges, the hand sphere's curve, and even the thin barrel cylinder tip all show a distinct near-black border rather than a raw gray-to-tan cut. Pixel sampling along the gun-vs-ground boundary (x:1400–2560, y:950–1300) found 821 dark boundary pixels, 733 of which (89%) fall within tolerance-15 of the stated outline color RGB(32,30,38), confirming both presence and correct hue of the inverted-hull pass — not just incidental anti-aliasing. The barrel is thinner than the slide's outline as expected given its 0.036-unit diameter, but it is not zero-width or missing as before; a left-edge scan across the cylinder found 41/42 tan-to-gun transitions had a dark pixel within 3px. Visually, the viewmodel now reads as the same low-poly/cel/outlined art direction as the created-character (left) and roaming NPC (right) figures rather than a pasted-in prop from a different style. One minor observation, not a failure: the outline is visibly thinner and slightly less saturated on the barrel underside than on the flat slide faces, consistent with the geometry note in the ticket, and does not read as inconsistent.
